# v3.09-dev

Groundwork for stronger protection against injected scripts. **Nothing changes
in this release** — the plumbing is in, switched off.

## Under the hood

- **Training Tracker now builds its Content-Security-Policy fresh for every
  request** instead of once when the app is built. That rule is what tells your
  browser which scripts a page is allowed to run, and building it per request
  lets each page tag its own scripts with a one-time value the browser can
  check — so anything that did not come from Training Tracker can be told apart
  from everything that did.

- **The rules your browser receives are byte-for-byte identical to the previous
  version.** This was verified across every kind of page, image, data request
  and error page the app serves — 27 in all — with no differences at all. The
  stricter rules arrive in the next release, as a separate change that can be
  turned off on its own.

- **New `CSP_MODE` setting** so an administrator can choose between the strict
  rules, a report-only trial and the previous behaviour. It is read on every
  request, so changing it takes a restart and **not** a rebuild — worth knowing,
  because rebuilding is the step that can run out of memory on a small server.
  See the README for how to use it.

## Fixed

- **A visitor could influence part of that browser rule by sending a crafted
  request.** Harmless under the previous policy, but it would not have been
  under the stricter one, so it is closed ahead of time.

- **Some unusual web addresses were being served without the browser rule at
  all** — misspelled icon and asset paths that fall between two internal lists.
  They only ever returned "not found" pages, so nothing was exposed, but they
  now get the same protection as every other address.
